chunks: What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “When should I perform the two rakʿahs of fajr?” He said: He said to me, “After the rising of fajr.” I said to him, “Indeed Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام instructed me to perform them before the rising of fajr.” He said, “O Abā Muḥammad, indeed the Shiʿah came to my father seeking right guidance, so he gave them fatwa with the bitter truth; and they came to me in a state of doubt, so I gave them fatwa in accordance with taqiyyah.”

key_terms.بِالتَّقِيَّةِ: in accordance with precautionary dissimulation to avoid harm
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ: the two rakʿahs associated with fajr prayer
key_terms.شُكَّاكًا: people in a state of doubt or uncertainty
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ: the onset or rising of dawn
key_terms.مُسْتَرْشِدِينَ: seeking right guidance and correct direction

ai.seo_question: When should the two rakʿahs of fajr be prayed, and why do different narrations give different timings?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the time of the two rakʿahs of fajr and records differing guidance attributed to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام and Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. The Imam explains that the difference in response was due to the condition of the questioners, stating that one answer reflected the bitter truth while another was given on the basis of taqiyyah.
